Print the objects table, one row per name

Source: R/find_objects.R
print.objects.Rd

Prints the table design_parameters() returns, and that print(design) shows under "Parameters and objects the design refers to", aggregated to one row per name with five columns. name is the name redesign() can change. value is a display snippet of what it currently holds. kind is how redesign() reads a bare replacement: scalar, vector, and list supply one design per element, while data, function, and other are single values. declared is TRUE when a declare_parameters() step declares the name and FALSE when the design reads it from the environment it was written in. steps lists the positions of the steps that read the name, which are the steps that would respond to a change.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'objects'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

x

(required) An objects table, as returned by design_parameters().

...

(optional) Ignored.

Value

x, invisibly.

Details

The underlying table has one row per name per step and carries the quosure and env columns that locate each binding; those are left out of the print.

Examples

tau <- 0.3
design <-
  declare_parameters(n_units = 100) +
  declare_model(N = n_units, U = rnorm(N), Y_Z_0 = U, Y_Z_1 = U + tau) +
  declare_inquiry(ATE = mean(Y_Z_1 - Y_Z_0)) +
  declare_assignment(Z = complete_ra(N))
design_parameters(design)
#>     name value   kind declared steps
#>  n_units   100 scalar     TRUE  1, 2
#>      tau   0.3 scalar    FALSE     2
